example.title: Segmented four-rod linear trap
example.reference: S. N. Miao et al., "Sympathetic cooling of a large ¹¹³Cd⁺ ion crystal with ⁴⁰Ca⁺ in a linear Paul trap", arXiv:2201.03377 (2022)
example.summary: Four round rods (R/r₀ = 1.145), each cut into end segments A, C and a trapping segment B. The drive is the paper's typical one for ⁴⁰Ca⁺. Compare the Trap tab's Mathieu q and a with the paper's.
published: rod diameter 14.2 mm, r₀ = 6.2 mm; segments A and C 20 mm, B 2z₀ = 40 mm
U_rf = 150 V on rods B2 and B4, Ω/2π = 1.961 MHz
U_end = 10 V on the end segments A and C
κ = 0.12, with a = 4QκU_end/(MΩ²z₀²), set in their simulation by matching simulated crystal images to experiment
should exceed 3 eV for stable trapping (a general requirement, not computed for this drive)
assumptions: 1 mm gaps between the segments (not stated).
Rods B1 and B3 grounded; the paper does not say. With ±75 V on the two pairs instead, the depth is 2.1 eV rather than 1.6 eV.
